evaluations.evidence: create a new game
evaluations.rationale: Backlog contains complementary capabilities (browse previous games PP-016, delete game PP-020), so creation is supported and not missing required counterparts.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators
evaluations.rationale: Complementary capability for estimators to join exists (PP-029), so invite + join are present.

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes item management (view PP-004, add PP-006, edit PP-007) needed to start rounds; no complementary capability missing for this story.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Item creation/import/copy capabilities exist (PP-006, PP-014, PP-015), so viewing items is supported.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selection operates on items that can be added/edited/deleted (PP-006, PP-007, PP-008); complementary item capabilities exist.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Editing and deleting items are present (PP-007, PP-008), so add is not orphaned.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Creation (PP-006) and deletion (PP-008) complement editing; no missing complementary requirement.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Item creation (PP-006) and editing (PP-007) exist, so deletion is not missing complementary functionality.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: This story presumes that estimators can give/submit estimates, but the backlog contains no explicit story for submitting or recording an estimator's estimate (e.g., "As an estimator, I want to give/submit an estimate"). That complementary capability is absent.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Computing/accepting an average requires recorded estimates from participants, yet there is no story specifying that estimators can submit/record their estimates; the submission capability is missing.

evaluations.evidence: "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: This depends on estimators showing/playing cards (submitting estimates). The backlog lacks a story for estimators to submit/play an estimate, so the necessary complementary capability is missing.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: This is a manual moderator action to record an agreed value and does not strictly require the (absent) estimator submission story to be present for the feature described.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Re-estimating assumes prior estimates were recorded and that estimators can submit estimates; the backlog lacks an explicit submission/storage story for estimator estimates.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Import complements other item-creation mechanisms (PP-006, PP-015); no required complementary capability is missing for importing stories.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/paste is an additional creation mechanism that does not require a missing complementary story.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing previous games is supported alongside create (PP-001) and view/export transcript stories (PP-017–PP-019); no complementary capability is absent for browsing.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game, so that I can see the stories and estimates
evaluations.rationale: Viewing transcripts requires that estimates were submitted and stored; the backlog lacks an explicit story for estimators to submit/record estimates, so the complementary storage/submission capability is missing.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting transcripts presumes transcripts include estimates; without a story for submitting/recording estimates, the required complementary capability is missing.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: CSV export expects stored stories and estimates; there is no story specifying how estimates are submitted/recorded, so a necessary complementary capability is absent.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game, so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: The story assumes stories and estimates are being stored; however, the backlog lacks an explicit story for estimators to submit/record estimates, so the complementary submission/storage capability is missing.

evaluations.evidence: create an account for the application
evaluations.rationale: Account creation is complemented by login (PP-022) and account management (PP-023, PP-024); no complementary capability is missing.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Login is paired with account creation (PP-021) and password reminder (PP-026); no missing complementary functionality evident.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Account modification complements creation and login stories; no necessary counterpart is missing.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account, so that account information and games are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Account deletion is a logical complement to account creation and management; related stories exist (PP-021) and no counterpart is missing.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Timezone display is a standalone UI concern and does not require other missing capabilities from the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminder complements account/login stories (PP-021, PP-022); no complementary capability is missing.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: This is a configuration option and does not presuppose a missing complementary capability; it can be implemented without additional absent stories.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Invitation limit complements invite/join functionality (PP-002, PP-029); no missing counterpart is evident.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name
evaluations.rationale: Joining is present and complements invitation (PP-002); no required counterpart is missing for joining itself.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Viewing the current item is supported by item management stories and does not strictly require the missing estimator-submission story to be implemented.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: This is a listing of items and is supported by add/import stories (PP-006, PP-014); no complementary capability is absent.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: This story assumes estimates are being submitted/recorded by estimators, but the backlog lacks an explicit story for submitting an estimate, so the complementary capability is missing.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Showing all estimates after submission presumes a submission mechanism; there is no story specifying that estimators can give/submit estimates, so that necessary capability is absent.

evaluations.evidence: be able to change my estimate up until the last person selects a card
evaluations.rationale: Changing an estimate presumes the ability to submit/play a card/estimate; the backlog contains no estimator-submission story, so the complementary capability is missing.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Viewing prior estimates requires that estimators' previous estimates were recorded; there is no story for submitting/storing estimates, so the complementary requirement is absent.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: This presumes estimates are submitted and attributed to users; the backlog lacks an explicit submit/record-estimate story, so the complementary capability is missing.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: A shared timer is an independent feature and does not strictly require the missing estimator-submission story to be implementable.

evaluations.evidence: two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Resetting based on "all play an estimate" requires a mechanism for playing/submitting estimates; no story exists that defines estimator submission, so the complementary capability is missing.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: This explicitly expects stored prior estimates; without a story for submitting/recording estimates, the required complementary capability is absent.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: The concept of "draws" and cards being played implies the ability to play/submit card estimates; the backlog lacks an explicit estimator submission story, so a necessary complementary capability is missing.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Changing an estimate presupposes the ability to submit an initial estimate; no story exists for estimator submission/playing an estimate, so the complementary capability is missing.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Displaying thumbnails near "where my cards are played" assumes card-play/submission behavior exists; the backlog has no story for submitting/playing estimates, so the complementary capability is missing.

evaluations.evidence: site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Standards compliance is an independent non-functional requirement and does not imply a missing complementary functional capability in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Documentation/glossary is an independent deliverable and does not reveal a missing complementary functional story.

evaluations.evidence: created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Database indexing supports performance but does not indicate a missing complementary functional capability in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: application function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Browser compatibility is non-functional and does not expose a missing complementary functional story.

evaluations.evidence: site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility compliance is non-functional and does not indicate missing functional counterparts.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Performance requirement is orthogonal to missing functional stories and does not expose absent complementary capabilities.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Unicode support is an implementation detail and does not imply missing functional capabilities in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: URL design is a UI/UX concern and does not point to missing functional stories required for features.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Error pages are a non-functional/user-experience requirement and do not indicate missing complementary functional stories.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Storing results presumes that estimates/results are being collected; the backlog does not include a story for estimators to submit/record their estimates, so the complementary submission/storage capability is missing.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Metrics can be derived from various existing events (games created PP-001, joins PP-029); while richer metrics might use estimates, the story as stated does not necessarily require a missing estimator-submission story.
